title: What does ISO 9001 require for competence under the 2015 and 2026 editions?
description: What ISO 9001 clause 7.2 requires for competence under the 2015 and 2026 editions, the new 7.3 awareness duties, what auditors check, and transition dates.
shortAnswer: ISO 9001 clause 7.2 requires an organization to determine the competence its people need, ensure they are competent through education, training or experience, close gaps and evaluate whether that worked, and retain evidence. ISO 9001:2026, published September 16, 2026, keeps the same clause structure. ISO says it adds awareness of quality culture and ethical behavior in clause 7.3. Certified organizations have three years to transition from ISO 9001:2015.
keyTakeaways: Clause 7.2 has four parts: determine competence, ensure competence, act and evaluate effectiveness, and retain documented information as evidence.
Training is one way to achieve competence; mentoring, reassignment and recruitment are others.

ISO 9001:2026 was published on September 16, 2026. ISO gives ISO 9001:2015 certificate holders three years to transition, and DQS reports that 2015 certificates are expected to remain valid until September 30, 2029.

ISO lists new awareness requirements on quality culture and ethical behavior (clause 7.3), stronger leadership emphasis on quality culture (clause 5.1) and a new explanatory Annex A; the clause structure is unchanged.
Auditors expect defined role competence and evidence of effectiveness, not only attendance records.
regulator: International Organization for Standardization (ISO), through accredited certification bodies
appliesTo: Organizations certified or seeking certification to ISO 9001
Suppliers whose customers or tenders require ISO 9001
Organizations using ISO 9001 as a quality governance reference

sections.heading: Which edition of ISO 9001 applies as at November 2026?

blocks.text: As at November 2026, both editions are in use during a transition. [ISO 9001:2026](https://www.iso.org/standard/9001) was published on September 16, 2026 as the sixth edition and replaces ISO 9001:2015. ISO states that organizations certified to ISO 9001:2015 [will have three years](https://www.iso.org/quality-management/iso-9001-2026) to move to the new edition without restarting certification. Certification body [DQS reports](https://www.dqsglobal.com/en/explore/blog/iso-9001-2026-transition) that ISO 9001:2015 certificates are expected to remain valid until September 30, 2029, subject to rules set by Global Accreditation Cooperation Incorporated (Global ACI, formerly the International Accreditation Forum).

For competence, the practical impact is limited. ISO confirms that the 2026 edition keeps the Harmonized Structure used across ISO management system standards, in which clause 7.2 is competence and clause 7.3 is awareness. The change that matters most for training owners is in awareness: ISO lists new clause 7.3 requirements on quality culture and ethical behavior. Organizations should confirm the exact clause wording against the purchased standard before updating procedures.

sections.heading: What changed in ISO 9001:2026 for competence and awareness?

blocks.text: The main change for people and training is a new awareness requirement on quality culture and ethical behavior in clause 7.3, supported by stronger leadership duties in clause 5.1. ISO's [summary of the 2026 edition](https://www.iso.org/quality-management/iso-9001-2026) does not list clause 7.2 competence among the main changes, and the clause numbering is unchanged.

blocks.caption: ISO 9001:2026 changes relevant to competence and awareness, as described by ISO (clause wording not reproduced)

blocks.text: The ISO 9001:2026 foreword, as shown in ISO's online preview, says quality culture and ethical behavior are addressed in requirements on leadership, awareness and the environment for the operation of processes. ISO also lists a clearer separation of risks and opportunities (clause 6.1) and a quality policy more explicitly linked to strategic direction (clause 5.2), and it carries forward the climate change consideration added to ISO 9001:2015 by the 2024 amendment. These can change a [training needs analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-training-needs-analysis), but they do not alter the four parts of clause 7.2 described below.

A practical transition sequence for competence and awareness is: compare current awareness content against the new clause 7.3 topics, identify roles that carry culture or ethics responsibilities, update role competence profiles and induction material, then record an effectiveness check before the transition audit. The [gap analysis](/platform/gap-analysis) approach is the same one ISO recommends for the transition as a whole.

Clause 7.2 requires competence to be defined, achieved, verified and evidenced for everyone doing work under the organization's control that affects the performance and effectiveness of the quality management system (QMS). The summary below follows ISO 9001:2015, the edition most certificates are held against during the transition. ISO's own summary of the 2026 edition does not list clause 7.2 among the main changes, and certification body summaries report no substantive change to it. In summary, the organization must:

items: determine the necessary competence of those persons
ensure those persons are competent on the basis of appropriate education, training or experience
where applicable, take actions to acquire the necessary competence and evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken
retain appropriate documented information as evidence of competence

blocks.text: The standard's note lists applicable actions such as providing training, mentoring or reassigning current employees, or hiring or contracting competent persons. This makes clause 7.2 an outcome requirement. A training course is only evidence of competence if the organization has defined what competence means for the role and checked that the person now meets it.

It covers persons doing work under the organization's control whose work affects QMS performance and effectiveness, which includes employees, contractors and outsourced personnel where the organization controls the work. It is not limited to quality staff: production operators, inspectors, customer service, designers, purchasing and managers can all affect conformity.

Clause 7.2 is linked to other parts of the standard. In ISO 9001:2015, clause 7.1.6 covers organizational knowledge, clause 7.3 covers awareness, and clause 8.4 covers control of externally provided processes, which can include supplier personnel competence. A [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) or [competency framework](/glossary/competency-framework) is the usual tool for bringing these together.

sections.heading: How is clause 7.3 awareness different from competence?

blocks.text: Awareness is what everyone must know; competence is what specific roles must be able to do. Under ISO 9001:2015, clause 7.3 requires people doing work under the organization's control to be aware of the quality policy, relevant quality objectives, their contribution to QMS effectiveness including the benefits of improved performance, and the implications of not conforming.

ISO states that the 2026 edition adds awareness requirements recognizing that quality depends on people's understanding of quality culture and ethical behavior. For training owners, that points to adding culture and ethics content to induction and refresher material, and being ready to show auditors that staff understand it, not only that they attended.

sections.heading: What evidence do auditors expect for clause 7.2?

blocks.text: Auditors expect to see defined competence for roles, records showing each person meets it, and evaluation of any actions taken to close gaps. The table below is an illustrative model that satisfies each part of the clause.

blocks.caption: Illustrative mapping: clause 7.2 element to learning design to evidence
head: Clause 7.2 element
What to design
Evidence to retain
rows: (a) Determine competence
Competence statements per role, drawn from process risks and product requirements
Approved role competence profiles with version and date
(b) Ensure competence
Assessment method for each competence, such as observation, practical test or verified qualification
Assessment records per person, qualifications, verified experience
(c) Act on gaps
Training, mentoring, reassignment or recruitment plan for each gap
Individual development plans and completion records
(c) Evaluate effectiveness
Re-assessment or performance measure after the action
Before and after results, supervisor sign off, defect or error trends
(d) Retain documented information
A single register linking people, roles, competences and evidence
Register export available for audit sampling

blocks.text: For step by step methods, see [how to build a competency framework](/guides/how-to-build-a-competency-framework), [how to conduct a training needs analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-training-needs-analysis) and [how to measure training effectiveness](/guides/how-to-measure-training-effectiveness).

sections.heading: What are common audit findings against clause 7.2?

blocks.text: The most frequent weakness is equating attendance with competence. Other typical gaps follow from the same cause: competence has not been defined, so it cannot be verified.

items: Role descriptions list duties but not the competence needed to perform them.
Training records exist but there is no evaluation of whether the training worked.
Temporary staff and contractors are missing from the competence register.
Competence requirements are not revised when processes, products or the standard change.
Evidence is held in separate systems, so sampling during an audit is slow and incomplete.

blocks.text: The transition to ISO 9001:2026 is a natural point to fix these gaps, since procedures and training will be reviewed anyway. Related management system requirements work the same way in [ISO/IEC 27001](/regulations/iso-27001-awareness-training-requirements) and [ISO 45001](/regulations/iso-45001-competence-and-awareness).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry defines role competencies as structured concepts with assessment points before training content is written, so clause 7.2(a) is answered by design and 7.2(b) to (d) by recorded assessment evidence. The same competence definitions can be mapped to ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 45001 at once.

faqs.q: Does ISO 9001 require a training matrix?
faqs.a: No. ISO 9001 does not name a training matrix. It requires the organization to determine competence, ensure people are competent, act on gaps, evaluate effectiveness and retain evidence. A training or skills matrix is a common way to hold that evidence, but any method that meets clause 7.2 is acceptable.

faqs.q: Do we need to change our competence process for ISO 9001:2026?
faqs.a: Probably not in structure. ISO confirms the clause structure is unchanged and does not list clause 7.2 among the main changes. Review awareness content instead, because ISO lists new clause 7.3 requirements on quality culture and ethical behavior. Check the purchased text and plan the change within the transition period agreed with your certification body.

faqs.q: How long do organizations have to transition to ISO 9001:2026?
faqs.a: ISO states that organizations certified to ISO 9001:2015 have three years to move to ISO 9001:2026 and do not need to restart certification. DQS reports that ISO 9001:2015 certificates are expected to remain valid until September 30, 2029, and that certificates issued against the 2015 edition during the transition have their validity cut off at that date.

faqs.q: How do you evaluate training effectiveness for clause 7.2?
faqs.a: Compare performance against the defined competence before and after the action. Methods include practical assessment, observation by a supervisor, reduced errors or nonconformities in the person's work, and customer feedback. Satisfaction surveys alone do not show that competence was achieved.

faqs.q: Can experience count as competence without training?
faqs.a: Yes. Clause 7.2 allows competence on the basis of education, training or experience. Where experience is relied on, retain evidence such as verified employment history, work samples, or an assessment by a competent person against the role's defined competence.
